title: Spare cycle pulse log — GPU warmup & scheduling notes
content:
Morning quick dump — spare-cycle pulse experiments and notes

Goal: see if short spare-cycle work (10–200ms) can be used to keep GPU kernels hot without impacting p50 tail for small / quick requests. Low-risk: run on canary nodes first.

Context / why:
- We see cold-kernel jitter on low-concurrency pods after 30s idle, resulting in micro-spikes at p99 (50–120ms extra).
- Dedicated warmup (full model load) is expensive; hypothesis: small no-op kernel dispatches keep kernels resident and reduce 99th tail.

Quick experiment plan (canary):
- Add lightweight noop dispatch every 15s on idle GPU worker loop (config flag: spare_cycle.pulse_interval_ms = 15000).
- Track: p50/p95/p99 token-latency, kernel-launch-time histogram, GPU SM utilization sample.
- Run for 2h windows during low traffic. Compare to sibling control set.

Commands / quick bits:
- deploy canary: ./infra/deploy.sh --stack=serving-canary --image=runtime:spare-pulse-20260312
- enable flag (local test): RUNTIME_FLAGS="spare_cycle.enabled=1 spare_cycle.pulse_interval_ms=15000" ./bin/runtime-server --dev
- collect traces: python tools/collect_traces.py --cluster canary --since 2h --out traces/pulse-canary.json

Preliminary observations (first 30m):
- p99 improved ~18% for short requests (<= 128 tokens) on first canary node, p50 unchanged.
- Kernel-launch-time median decreased 12ms, tail decreased more (some 30–45ms spikes removed).
- Slight increase in idle GPU SM utilization (~1.3% avg) — OK for Dedicated but might matter for shared nodes.

Open questions / risks: 
- Does continuous pulse interfere with batching heuristics? Observed one case where microbatches got pushed by 2–3ms. Need to instrument batch aggregator buckets.
- Memory pressure? Not observed yet, but edge case if other processes allocate transiently.
- Billing and cost: if shared-hosting, increased GPU cycles could raise unit costs — need econ estimate via Optimize team.

Next-actions (short):
- [ ] Add instrumentation: batch-aggregator latency counters tagged with spare_cycle flag (ticket JIRA-RT-1342).
- [ ] Run A/B for 24h across 3 canary pods in eu-west-1. (Assign: Maya)
- [ ] Add safety: pulse suppressed when queue length > 4 to avoid interfering with bursts.
- [ ] Draft short playbook for Dedicated customers: pros/cons and opt-in config. (Assign: me + Rohan)

Kernel-level notes (reminders for later deep-dive):
- Check kernel spinup path in src/runtime/kernel_launch.cc around line 412 — big TODO: add per-kernel timestamp before launch and after first warp executed.
- Explore using cuLaunchKernel async warm path vs dispatching trivial matmul to keep SMs active. Pro/con: async warm path might be driver-dependent.
- NUMA/pinning: ensure pulse thread pinned to same NUMA node as worker on multi-socket nodes — else warmup may trigger cross-socket penalties.

Telemetry snippet to add to trace (proto field suggestions):
- spare_cycle.pulse_sent_ts
- spare_cycle.kernel_launch_latency_ms
- spare_cycle.pulse_suppressed_reason = {high_queue, already_warming, maintenance}

Hypotheses to test (measurable):
1) Pulse reduces kernel-launch tail by >= 20ms for short requests (<=128 tokens).
2) Pulse does not increase average tail for batched requests (>512 tokens) by more than 5ms.
3) Pulse impact on GPU cost per 1M tokens < 0.5% (ask Optimize for model profile numbers).

Notes to self:
- If we see regression on batches, add per-route opt-out in routing policy (route.metadata.spare_cycle_optout).
- Consider running an alternative: prefix-cache warming instead of kernel ping (might be cheaper if many repeated prefixes).

Meeting TODOs / folks to sync:
- Quick sync with Maya 11:30am — run review of 2h pilot.
- Drop notes to Optimize: email thread summarizing first 30m numbers, CC: Nikhil.
- Follow up with SRE: check rollout/canary guardrails, porto-limit on canary nodes.

Random scratch (brain dump):
- If we eventually make spare_cycle a user-visible knob, name it something friendly like "keep-warm" or "idle-warmup" in API docs.
- Could expose level: off/low/medium/high with different intervals and noop kernel complexity.
- Danger: customers misconfiguring on shared tier -> add guard: max_pulse_rate_per_node enforced by control-plane.

End-of-day quick log:
- 16:00 check-in: A/B started 14:05, looks stable. Need 12–24h to be confident.
- Left notes in PR 987 for reviewers about NUMA pinning changes and unit tests.

-- oliver
